depends_on: Morrison 1980: every eventually positive Fibonacci sequence is a row tail of the Wythoff array
notes: True up to sign and known: Fibonacci tails are Wythoff rows (Morrison 1980); D(i) = F(i+1)^2 - F(i)F(i+2) alternates sign so the characteristic is constant; D_F3(i) = D_F1(i) D_F2(j) (norm in Z[phi]). F3 may be negative (Fibonacci, j = 1: F3(i) = -F(i-1)), so the row is that of |F3|. Lean (core): char_const, F3_fib, D_F3, char_F3, F3_negative_example. Outside Lean: Morrison's theorem, row n has characteristic a(n), eventual constant sign of F3.

sources.cite: D. R. Morrison, A Stolarsky array of Wythoff pairs, in A Collection of Manuscripts Related to the Fibonacci Sequence (1980) 134-136
